:::{#exm-markov-chain-noisy-copies}
#### A chain of noisy copies is a Markov chain
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

In @exm-entropy-chain-rule-n-copies,
each of $X_2$ and $X_3$ is a noisy copy of the variable before it.
So $X_3$ depends on $X_1$ only through $X_2$.
The chunk builds the [joint probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf) of $(X_1, X_2, X_3)$
and checks the defining equation of the chain $X_1 \to X_2 \to X_3$ for each value of $X_2$.

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
flip <- 0.2
copy <- matrix(
  data = c(1 - flip, flip, flip, 1 - flip),
  nrow = 2
)
joint <- array(data = 0, dim = c(2, 2, 2))
for (x1 in 1:2) {
  for (x2 in 1:2) {
    for (x3 in 1:2) {
      joint[x1, x2, x3] <- 0.5 * copy[x1, x2] * copy[x2, x3]
    }
  }
}
gaps <- numeric(2)
for (x2 in 1:2) {
  slice <- joint[, x2, ]
  given_x2 <- slice / sum(slice)
  product <- outer(rowSums(given_x2), colSums(given_x2))
  gaps[x2] <- max(abs(given_x2 - product))
}
gaps
```

Both gaps are zero up to rounding,
so $X_1$ and $X_3$ are [conditionally independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-cind) given $X_2$.

:::
